description: Generated by `npm run sync` from the UI.define() calls in recipes/web/*.js. Do not hand-edit.

components.label: Absorb drops
components.description: Falling drops caught by a target that adopts the colour of whichever it catches, using a swept band test so fast drops cannot step over it.

seed.controls: Where the opening drops sit and which colours they carry. A different seed is a different first frame with the same behaviour.

catcherWidth.controls: Width of the target: how forgiving the catch is. Wide reads as a bucket, narrow as a precise hit.

dropRadius.controls: Drop size. Small drops read as rain, large ones as tokens or coins.

fallSpeed.controls: Starting fall speed: how quickly a burst reaches the catcher.

accel.controls: How much each drop speeds up per frame. It is what spreads a burst out on the way down instead of letting it land as a rank.
accel.unswept: compounds frame over frame while drops fall; the single frame painted under reduced motion holds one step of it, which no still can show

seedDrops.controls: How many drops are on screen when it first paints, so the frame shows the mechanic before anyone clicks.

components.label: Acorn hoard
components.description: A count drawn as a tapering pile of objects, with a character whose feet rise as the pile grows.

count.controls: The number being shown, as acorns in a tapering pile; the character stands higher as it grows.

breaks.above: Past the rows' total capacity (24) the pile is full and further count is not drawn: say the number in text.

size.controls: Pixel scale of each acorn: how big the pile reads next to the character.

spriteScale.controls: Pixel scale of the character on the pile.

pose.controls: The character's expression: how the count should feel (plenty, celebration, neutral, running low).

components.label: Bar chart
components.description: SVG bars with a 2px surface gap, data-end rounding only, and a hidden table of the real values.

radius.controls: Rounding on the data end of each bar only. Softens the chart without detaching bars from their baseline.

breaks.below: Swept: 0 to 2px changes under 0.05% of the chart at this bar width, so rounding only reads from ~4px.
breaks.above: Past half the bar width the cap turns into a pill and short bars read as floating.

height.controls: Chart height: how much vertical room the values get, and so how readable small differences are.

color.controls: Bar fill. One colour for one series; the 2px gaps are drawn in the surface colour.

components.label: Blob shape
components.description: Seeded organic blob from a closed cubic Bézier — reproducible, and smooth across the seam.

seed.controls: Which blob: a different seed is a different silhouette with the same smoothness, and the same seed is always the same one.

points.controls: Number of lobes around the edge. Few reads as a pebble, many as a splat.

wobble.controls: How far points stray from the circle: 0 is a circle, high is a lumpy, organic shape.

breaks.above: Past ~0.5 lobes can fold back over each other and the outline pinches.

components.label: Canvas chart
components.description: Data-driven 2D chart (line or bar), DPR-aware, resizes with its container.

type.controls: Line for a trend over an ordered axis, bar for comparing separate amounts.

data.controls: The series: labels on the x axis, values scaled to the tallest.
data.cost: linear in points; redraws on resize

color.controls: Series colour. Accepts a CSS variable, so the chart follows the page's theme.

components.label: Click to split
components.description: Gravity-and-friction balls that divide into two smaller ones where clicked, with a predictive floor test so fast bounces do not stutter.

seed.controls: Where the balls start and their sizes and colours. A different seed is a different opening frame.

count.controls: How many balls start on screen: a few toys or a crowd.

gravity.controls: Downward pull per frame: floaty at low values, heavy at high.
gravity.unswept: acts over time as balls fall; under reduced motion the loop never starts, so no still frame shows it

friction.controls: Horizontal damping per frame: how long balls keep drifting sideways.
friction.unswept: acts over time; under reduced motion the loop never starts, so no still frame shows it

restitution.controls: Bounce: the share of speed kept off the floor. Low is a thud, near 1 is a rubber ball.
restitution.unswept: acts only on a bounce, over time; no still frame shows it

splitRatio.controls: How unevenly a clicked ball divides: 0.5 is two equal halves, higher gives one clearly bigger child.
splitRatio.unswept: acts only when a ball is clicked; the sweep has no pointer

minRadius.controls: Smallest ball. Sets the size range at the start, and below it a clicked ball vanishes instead of splitting.

components.label: Companion perch
components.description: Places a decorative sprite in whitespace it measured inside real components — and places none at all rather than covering text.

count.controls: How many companions may perch. Each needs a component with a whole body's worth of free space, so fewer may appear.

breaks.above: Swept: the preview layout has room for two; a third finds no free space and sits out, as designed.

count.cost: one layout probe pass per companion

spriteSize.controls: Size of the companion. Bigger needs more whitespace, so it perches less often.

pad.controls: Clearance kept from text and controls around the perch.

key.controls: A stable name for the placement, so the same page puts the companion in the same spot each visit.

components.label: Donut chart
components.description: Proportion ring assembled from dash-offset circles — no arc-path maths, no large-arc bugs.

thickness.controls: Ring width: thin reads as a delicate gauge, thick as a solid share chart.

breaks.above: Near half the size the hole closes and it becomes a pie.

centerLabel.controls: The figure in the hole: usually the total.

components.label: Duotone filter
components.description: Two-colour image treatment via true luminance plus a two-stop transfer table.

shadow.controls: The colour the darkest tones become. Usually the darker brand colour.
shadow.cost: none — one filter, run by the renderer

highlight.controls: The colour the lightest tones become. Usually a pale brand tint, or white for contrast.

signature.why: a luminance matrix feeding a per-channel transfer table is the duotone recipe

components.label: Flow field
components.description: Particles steered by a precomputed noise angle grid, painting trails. One static pass under reduced motion.

particles.controls: How many trails are drawn. Sets the density of the texture: sparse reads as strokes, dense as a woven surface.
particles.cost: linear — every particle steps every frame (and 260 times when primed)

speed.controls: Step length per frame. In the primed (and reduced-motion) image it sets how long each trail runs: short reads as hair, long as flowing lines.

scale.controls: Noise cell size: how far the flow curves before it turns. Small scale is turbulent, large is calm and sweeping.
scale.cost: none — the angle grid is precomputed once

seed.controls: Which field is drawn. A different seed is a different composition with the same character.

components.label: Glow filter
components.description: Neon halo from feGaussianBlur merged under the source, with a widened filter region so it is not clipped.

strength.controls: Blur radius of the halo: how far the light spreads past the shape.

breaks.above: Large blurs thin out; past ~12 the halo reads as fog rather than light.

strength.cost: grows with blur radius; filters repaint on every change

layers.controls: How many copies of the blur are stacked under the shape: one is soft, more is intense, like a neon tube.

signature.why: a blur merged back under its own source is the glow recipe

components.label: Gooey blobs
components.description: Blur-plus-alpha-contrast filter that merges nearby shapes into one gooey mass.

blur.controls: How far apart shapes start to merge: the blur radius sets the reach of each halo, and so the size of the bridge between them.

breaks.above: Past ~20 the halos swamp the shapes and everything melts into one round mass.

contrast.controls: Alpha contrast: how hard the edge snaps back after blurring. Low is soft and smoky, high is crisp liquid.

offset.controls: Alpha offset: where the edge is cut. More negative shrinks the shapes and thins the bridge; nearer 0 fattens both.

signature.why: a heavy blur feeding an alpha-contrast colour matrix is the gooey recipe itself

components.label: Halftone
components.description: Print-style dot screen on a rotated lattice, with each dot sized by its cell average.

cell.controls: Dot pitch. Sets how coarse the screen reads — the single knob between "a printed image" and "a pattern of circles".

breaks.below: Clamped to 2 in apply(). Near 2 the radius falls under the 0.25px cull and light cells drop out rather than shrink.
breaks.above: Past ~32 on the 220x150 preview source there are too few cells to carry the image.

cell.cost: none — the per-cell average reads every source pixel exactly once at any cell size

angle.controls: Screen angle. At 0 the lattice is axis-aligned and reads as pixelation; rotating it is the entire difference between print and mosaic.

invert.controls: Swaps ink for paper — dot radius tracks lightness instead of darkness.

components.snippet:
// Paint or drawImage onto the canvas first, then:
UIHalftone.apply(canvasEl, { cell: 8, angle: 45, ink: '#0b1d12' });

components.label: Heatmap grid
components.description: Contribution-style grid with a quantised colour scale and a matching legend — five readable steps, not a continuous ramp.

columns.controls: Columns of the grid (weeks, in a contribution graph): the time span shown.

cell.controls: Cell size: how much each value reads as a tile versus a dot.

gap.controls: Space between cells. Tight reads as a texture, wide as separate days.

radius.controls: Cell corner rounding: square and technical at 0, soft and friendly near half the cell.

components.label: Hit grid
components.description: Canvas cell grid whose column count is arithmetic rather than breakpoints, and which resolves the hovered cell by division instead of a hit-test loop.

cell.controls: Cell pitch. The column count follows from it and the container width, so this one number replaces breakpoints.
cell.cost: linear in cells to draw; hover lookup is one division at any size

gap.controls: Space between cells; also part of the pitch the column count is computed from.

lineWidth.controls: Cell outline weight: light reads as a calendar, heavy as a board.

components.label: Icon
components.description: Monoline stroke icon set, 24×24 viewBox, currentColor.

size.controls: Icon size. The 1.75px stroke stays constant, so small icons read bolder than large ones.

class.controls: A class on the <svg> for the caller's own CSS (colour, alignment).
class.unswept: a hook for the caller's stylesheet; the recipe styles nothing by it, so no frame of its own can show it

components.label: Image dither
components.description: Floyd–Steinberg error diffusion — few colours, no banding. Operates in place on a canvas.

levels.controls: Colours per channel. 2 is the classic 1-bit look; more levels approach the original image.

breaks.below: Below 2 there is nothing to dither between; it is clamped to 2.

mono.controls: Greyscale first (newspaper, e-ink) or dither each channel (a few-colour retro photo).

components.snippet:
// Paint or drawImage onto the canvas first, then:
UIImageDither.apply(canvasEl, { levels: 2, mono: true });

components.label: LED matrix
components.description: Departure-board text as lit dots, sampled from the browser’s own glyph rasteriser — every font and language for free, no bitmap font.

text.controls: The message on the board. Any font and language works, because the browser draws the glyphs.

rows.controls: Dots per character height: resolution. Few rows read as chunky hardware, many as a smooth sign.

breaks.below: Under ~6 rows letters lose their counters and stop being legible.

dot.controls: Dot size: the scale of the board on the page.

scroll.controls: Whether text that does not fit scrolls across like a ticker.
scroll.unswept: motion: under reduced motion the board stops scrolling, as designed, so no still frame shows it

components.label: Liquid fill text
components.description: Text that fills like a glass to a value — a seamless looping wave inside an SVG mask. The fill level is the data.

value.controls: The fill level, 0 to 1. This is the data: the word shows how full the thing is.

amplitude.controls: Wave height on the surface: calm at low values, sloshing at high.

wavelength.controls: Distance between crests: short is choppy, long is a gentle swell.

animate.controls: Whether the surface moves. The level never moves; only the wave does.
animate.unswept: motion: under reduced motion the surface stops, as designed, so no still frame shows it

signature.why: a translating wave inside a text mask is the liquid-fill recipe

components.label: Liquid glass
components.description: Frosted panel: backdrop blur warped by a noise displacement map, with a pointer-tracked highlight.

blur.controls: Frosting: how much the backdrop is blurred. Low is clear glass, high is frosted.

breaks.above: Swept: past ~12px the preview backdrop is already fully smoothed, so more blur changes nothing visible; the useful ceiling depends on how fine the backdrop is.

blur.cost: backdrop-filter repaints with everything behind the panel

distortion.controls: How much the glass bends what is behind it: thickness, read as refraction.
distortion.cost: a displacement filter on the panel

signature.why: noise, softened, then displacing the source is the refraction chain this recipe encapsulates

components.label: Noise grain
components.description: Resolution-independent film grain from feTurbulence — no tiled PNG, no extra request.

baseFrequency.controls: Grain size: high is fine film grain, low is blotchy paper tooth.
baseFrequency.cost: none — generated by the renderer at paint resolution

opacity.controls: How strongly the grain shows. Keep it subtle: grain should be felt before it is seen.

breaks.below: Swept: under ~0.11 the grain changes no pixel by more than 4/255 on this swatch; it is invisible, not subtle.

numOctaves.controls: Layers of finer detail on top of the base grain. Only the second octave is visible, and only on coarse texture: 1 is smooth mottling, 2 adds tooth. At the default fine grain no octave step changes anything.

breaks.above: Swept: past 2 octaves the added detail is below a pixel even on coarse grain (0.05); 3 and 4 only cost more.

blend.controls: How grain combines with what is under it: multiply darkens (paper), overlay and soft-light keep contrast (film), normal lays grey over it.

signature.why: fractal noise desaturated to grey and used as a layer is the grain recipe

components.label: Particle field
components.description: Drifting points linked by distance-faded lines. DPR-aware; paints one static frame under reduced motion.

seed.controls: Where the points start. A different seed is a different constellation with the same density.

count.controls: How many points. The mesh gets denser fast, because links grow with the square of the count.

breaks.above: Above ~300 the pair loop (O(n²)) costs too much per frame; use another technique.

count.cost: quadratic: every pair is tested each frame

linkDist.controls: How close two points must be to be linked: sparse dots at low values, a web at high.

speed.controls: Drift speed: how restless the field feels.
speed.unswept: motion: sets velocities only; under reduced motion one frame is painted, so no still frame shows it

dotRadius.controls: Point size: whether the points or the lines carry the image.

components.label: Path draw-on
components.description: A stroke that paints itself on, measured with getTotalLength(). Renders complete and static under reduced motion.

shape.controls: Which path draws itself. Any path works; these show a flourish, a confirmation tick and a signature.

duration.controls: How long the stroke takes to draw: quick reads as a flourish, slow as handwriting.
duration.unswept: motion: under reduced motion the path is drawn complete at once, as designed, so no still frame shows it

strokeWidth.controls: Line weight of the drawn stroke.

loop.controls: Whether the drawing repeats or draws once and stays.
loop.unswept: motion: under reduced motion nothing animates, so no still frame shows it

signature.why: a path whose dasharray equals its own length is the draw-on recipe

components.label: Pattern hatch
components.description: Hatch, crosshatch and dot fills that survive greyscale, print and forced-colors — the texture encoding.

size.controls: Tile size: the spacing between hatch lines (and dot pitch). Small reads as a tone, large as visible stripes.

breaks.below: Under ~3px with weight 1.5 the lines merge into a flat fill and the texture stops encoding anything.

size.cost: none — one <pattern> tile, drawn by the renderer

weight.controls: Line weight: how dark the hatch reads. Heavier lines carry further and survive print; thin ones read as a light tone.

breaks.above: Near the tile size the lines fill the tile and the hatch becomes a solid.

angle.controls: Rotates the whole pattern. Distinguishes two series that share a hatch kind.

signature.why: a user-space tiled pattern used as a fill is the texture-encoding recipe

components.label: Pixel sprite
components.description: Character sprites as row-maps blitted to canvas — variants are pixel patches, not extra PNGs. Crisp at any integer scale.

pose.controls: The character's expression and body: each is a pixel patch on one base map.

mood.controls: An overlay on the pose: a worried brow, a despair cloud, sleep, fire. Blink is an animation and shows only in motion.

scale.controls: Whole-pixel scale of the sprite. Integers only stay crisp.

breaks.below: Fractional scales blur or skip pixel rows; keep it an integer.

animate.unswept: motion: under reduced motion the sprite holds still, as designed, so no still frame shows it

components.label: Progress ring
components.description: Determinate circular progress from one stroked circle and a dash offset. Announces as a progressbar.

value.controls: The progress, 0 to 100: how much of the ring is filled.

thickness.controls: Stroke width: thin is a delicate indicator, thick a bold status.

showValue.controls: Whether the number sits in the middle. The value is announced either way.

signature.why: a dash-offset circle is the ring recipe itself, however the arc got there

components.label: Proximity dots
components.description: A drifting dot field where radius is driven by pointer distance, rate-limited so the response trails rather than snaps.

seed.controls: Where the dots start and their resting sizes. A different seed is a different field with the same density.

count.controls: How many dots: a sparse scatter or a dense surface.

range.controls: How far from the pointer dots respond: the size of the swell around the cursor.
range.unswept: responds only to a pointer; the sweep has none

minRadius.controls: Resting dot size, before the pointer comes near.

maxRadius.controls: How big a dot grows under the pointer: a gentle swell or a bold bloom.
maxRadius.unswept: reached only near a pointer; the sweep has none

speed.unswept: motion: under reduced motion nothing drifts, as designed, so no still frame shows it

step.controls: How fast a dot catches up with its target size: low leaves a slow wake behind the pointer, high snaps.
step.unswept: acts over frames while the pointer moves; the sweep has no pointer

components.label: Radial gauge
components.description: Partial-sweep gauge from a real arc path, with the large-arc flag computed rather than guessed.

value.controls: The reading, 0 to 1, as a share of the arc.

sweep.controls: How much of a circle the dial spans: 180 is a speedometer half, 270 the classic meter, near 360 a ring.

components.label: Scratch off
components.description: Reveal-by-erasing via destination-out compositing, with a keyboard-reachable Reveal button as the real path.

radius.controls: Brush size of the scratch: small makes it a careful reveal, large a quick swipe.
radius.unswept: acts only while someone scratches; the sweep has no pointer

threshold.controls: Share of the surface that must be cleared before the rest reveals itself.
threshold.unswept: acts only after scratching; the sweep has no pointer

width.cost: alpha sampling grows with area (every 8th pixel)

components.label: Skeleton shimmer
components.description: Loading placeholder with a composited gradient sweep, one live-region announcement, and a flat fallback under reduced motion.

lines.controls: How many text lines the placeholder stands in for. Match the content that is coming.

avatar.controls: Whether a round avatar block leads the lines, as in a comment or a profile row.

lineHeight.controls: Height of each line block: match the type size that will replace it.

lastLineWidth.controls: Width of the last line, so the block reads as a paragraph rather than a grid of bars.

components.label: Sparkline
components.description: Word-sized trend line: no axes, no grid, no legend. Scales by viewBox with a non-scaling stroke.

strokeWidth.controls: Line weight. It stays the same at any size (non-scaling stroke).

width.controls: Length of the line: a word's worth beside the number it qualifies.

height.controls: Height: about one line of text, so it reads as typography rather than a chart.

fill.controls: Shades the area under the line, which reads as a quantity rather than a rate.

showLast.controls: A dot on the last value, which is usually the number the line sits next to.

signature.why: a non-scaling stroked polyline in a small viewBox is the sparkline construction

components.label: Spirograph
components.description: Hypotrochoid and epitrochoid curves from two radii and a pen offset — generative art with no randomness and no assets.

R.controls: Radius of the fixed ring: with r it sets how many petals the figure has (R / gcd(R, r)).
R.cost: path length, and so steps, grows with R / gcd(R, r)

r.controls: Radius of the rolling circle: small r against R gives many fine loops, near R few broad ones.

d.controls: Pen offset from the rolling centre: small is a gentle rosette, past r the curve loops back on itself.

epi.controls: Roll outside the ring (epitrochoid, an open flower) instead of inside (hypotrochoid, a dense star).

components.label: Squiggle wobble
components.description: Hand-drawn wobble: animated fractal-noise displacement. Honours prefers-reduced-motion.

scale.controls: Displacement strength: how far lines wobble from where they were drawn. Low is a careful hand, high is a scribble.

breaks.above: Past ~30 thin strokes break apart into fragments.

baseFrequency.controls: Wobble frequency: low is a slow, wavy hand; high is a nervous jitter.

speed.controls: How often the noise is re-seeded: the boil rate of the line.
speed.unswept: motion: under reduced motion the re-seeding stops, as designed, so no still frame shows it

animate.controls: Whether the line boils (re-seeds) or holds one wobble.
animate.unswept: motion: under reduced motion it holds one wobble, as designed, so no still frame shows it

signature.why: a turbulence map feeding a displacement map is the wobble recipe itself

components.label: Star rating
components.description: Fractional star fill via a clipped overlay — 3.6 renders as 3.6, and announces as a number.

value.controls: The rating, filled to the exact fraction: 3.6 shows as 3.6, not rounded to a half.

max.controls: How many stars the scale has.

components.snippet: container.innerHTML = UIStarRating.render({ value: 3.6, max: 5, size: 28 });

components.label: Three instanced grid
components.description: Thousands of lit, individually-transformed cubes in one draw call via InstancedMesh.

side.controls: Cubes per side of the grid (side² in total): a small block or a city.
side.cost: one draw call at any count; per-instance matrices grow with side²

spacing.controls: Distance between cube centres: packed into a surface, or separate blocks.

cubeSize.controls: Size of each cube, against the spacing: gaps show when it is smaller, cubes touch when it matches.

amplitude.controls: Height of the wave the cubes rise and fall on: flat at 0, a rolling landscape at high values.

requires: three@0.128.0 UMD build, exposed as the global THREE

components.label: Three point cloud
components.description: Thousands of particles as one THREE.Points draw call, distributed uniformly on a sphere.

seed.controls: Which scatter of points. A different seed is a different cloud with the same shape.

count.controls: How many points: a faint dusting or a dense shell.
count.cost: one draw call at any count; the buffer grows linearly

size.controls: Point size, in scene units: dust at small values, beads at large.

breaks.below: Swept: at the preview's camera distance anything under ~0.03 draws at the 1px minimum, so 0.011 and 0.022 look the same.

radius.controls: Radius of the sphere the points sit on.

sizeAttenuation.controls: Near points draw larger, which is what reads as depth. Off gives a flat starfield.

requires: three@0.128.0 UMD build, exposed as the global THREE

components.label: Three scene
components.description: Auto-rotating 3D mesh mounted into a container div.

geometry.controls: The object: a faceted gem, a knot, or a box.

color.controls: Material colour, lit by the scene.

wireframe.controls: Draw edges only: technical and light, instead of a solid lit object.

requires: three@0.128.0 UMD build, exposed as the global THREE

components.label: Three shader plane
components.description: Minimal correct scaffold for raw GLSL: orthographic camera, clip-space quad, live time and resolution uniforms.

scale.controls: Pattern scale of the shader: large, slow forms at low values, busy detail at high.

speed.controls: How fast the pattern moves (time multiplier).
speed.unswept: motion: under reduced motion time is frozen at zero, as designed, so no still frame shows it

colorA.controls: The darker of the two colours the pattern blends between.

colorB.controls: The lighter colour: what the pattern's highlights become.

requires: three@0.128.0 UMD build, exposed as the global THREE

components.label: Three wireframe globe
components.description: Wireframe sphere with lat/lon markers in one InstancedMesh — including the polar-angle conversion everyone gets wrong.

segments.controls: Wireframe density: few segments read as a lattice, many as a fine globe.

markerSize.controls: Size of the location markers: subtle dots or bold pins.
markerSize.cost: one draw call for all markers

rotation.controls: Which side of the globe faces the viewer (the resting longitude).

requires: three@0.128.0 UMD build, exposed as the global THREE

components.label: VHS glitch
components.description: Chromatic aberration, torn bands and scanlines over any canvas — the tape look, in three getImageData passes and no shader.

split.controls: Chromatic aberration: how far red and blue are pushed apart. This does most of the tape look.

bands.controls: How many torn horizontal slabs: a clean signal at 0, a damaged tape at many.

tear.controls: How far each torn slab is displaced sideways.

scanline.controls: Darkness of the scanlines drawn over everything: faint CRT texture or heavy bars.

components.label: Wave divider
components.description: Section divider from a generated sine path; stretches to any width via preserveAspectRatio="none".

amplitude.controls: Wave height: a gentle ripple or a bold swell between sections.

cycles.controls: How many waves span the width: one lazy curve or a busy ripple.

flip.controls: Turn the wave upside down, for the bottom edge of a section rather than the top.
